notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found for the open-mode tier after a failed OPEN). Not implemented: one path of the rule's "any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure applicable to the file-name". §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR5 e makes a USE ... ON EXTEND procedure applicable to "any file open in the extend mode or in the process of being opened in the extend mode" (b, c and d say the same of INPUT, OUTPUT and I-O). FileConnector.OpenOnceEntered records the mode of an OPEN that fails and nothing clears it until a successful CLOSE, so FileConnector.OpenModeView still answers that mode to the open-mode tier (EmitScopeTiers) for every later statement: a WRITE to a file that is not open (48), executed after a failed OPEN EXTEND, runs the USE ... ON EXTEND procedure, where the same WRITE before any OPEN (and after a CLOSE) runs none; the CLOSE that follows (42) runs it too. The mechanism is the USE statement's, reaches every I-O statement of the three file modules at every edition (probed the same at --std 2023), and is recorded once more on 1985-GR-VII.4.4.4-11 of this slice. Implemented at 85, everything else of §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR10: SequentialIoEmitter.EmitWrite emits the runtime WRITE, then the FILE STATUS store, then EmitUseHook, whose __IoCheck (EmitUseMachinery) returns on a successful status and otherwise runs the file-name USE procedure, else the open-mode one, and returns to the statement after the WRITE; the END-OF-PAGE and NOT END-OF-PAGE statements are guarded by IoStatusClass.Successful, so an unsuccessful WRITE runs neither. SequentialConnector.WriteRecord and WriteAdvancingRecord answer 48 for a file not open in the output or extend mode and 44 for a record outside the RECORD IS VARYING bounds before anything reaches the medium. No edition arm; at 85 no EC-I-O checking exists, so the hook is always the plain one. Probed at --std 85: a WRITE FROM with both END-OF-PAGE phrases to a closed LINAGE file (48) runs the file-name USE procedure and neither phrase, after the FROM move; a DEPENDING ON value of 2 and of 11 against FROM 3 TO 10 (44) run it; a WRITE to a file open for input runs the USE ... ON INPUT procedure and one to a file open I-O the USE ... ON I-O procedure; with no applicable procedure and a FILE STATUS item the next statement runs. The witness fails a WRITE to a file open for input (48) under a file-name USE procedure.

next.reason: 1985 (1993 amendment): on an unsuccessful WRITE 'the I-O status of the file-name ... is updated and control is transferred according to the rules of the USE statement following the execution of any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure applicable'. §2023:14.9.51.4 GR15 and GR1 set the I-O status of the write file connector and send control through 9.1.12; §2023:9.1.12 GR2 names the USE declarative, selected by §2023:14.9.49.4 GR3 and GR6, and §2023:14.9.49.4 GR7 returns control after it. But 9.1.12 puts first 'Statements in a WHEN phrase of an active PERFORM statement' (§2023:9.1.12 GR1), and GR6 runs the USE procedure only when the WRITE is outside an exception-checking PERFORM or no WHEN matched: a WRITE in an exception-checking PERFORM with a matching WHEN runs no USE procedure. 2023 accepts that program, 1985 refuses it, and the result differs: a case added, so CHANGED. (GR15's record-area words are another 1985 rule's.)
